blocks.text: What an ai assistant for hotel revenue managers does on a Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant that sits on your Mac. You hold ⌥⌘ and ask a question about what is on screen. Lazur answers out loud. It points at the thing you mean, or it walks you through the next step. It works in any app that is open, which matters because a revenue manager's day is spread across many windows.

Lazur guides, points, explains, answers out loud, drafts and types text. It does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. You still make every change. Lazur helps you find it and understand it.
Where a revenue manager's day goes

Revenue managers spend less time on revenue than their title suggests. An HSMAI study, as reported by Hospitality Upgrade in fall 2024, says they devote less than half their time to generating revenue. The article gives no exact percentage and does not name the study year. Read it as a clear direction, not a precise measure.

The biggest named block is forecasting. The same article says revenue managers spend nearly 12 full-time weeks a year producing forecasts and budgets. Forecasts depend on clean data from several sources at once. A late export or a missing column costs more time than it looks like.
The rest of the week goes to manual work. The article lists these tasks.

items: Moving data into reports by hand
Logging in and out of several tools
Answering check-in calls and emails from sales and marketing
Updating the hotel website or the central reservation system

blocks.text: Survey data points the same way. In RoomPriceGenie's 2026 survey of 450 senior revenue decision-makers, 45% said operational teams lack confidence interpreting revenue data. Only 36% review their pricing strategy at least monthly. The survey comes from a company that sells pricing software, and it gives no fielding dates or time-spent figures. Use it as a signal, not a benchmark.
Excel, Google Sheets and Gmail on Mac: where the work lives

Most of your rate and channel tools run in a browser, so Lazur helps with them through Chrome or Safari. The Mac apps you will use most are Excel for forecasts, Google Sheets for shared pickup files, and Gmail or Outlook for sales requests. Each one needs a different kind of help.

For Excel, Microsoft says that starting with the September 2025 update, version 16.101, macOS Sonoma or later is required to keep getting Office updates for Mac. Microsoft's notes for Excel 2024 for Mac list dynamic charts and dynamic arrays among its headline features. To check your version, open Excel > About Excel. If your Mac runs an older system, ask IT before you plan a month around a spreadsheet.

blocks.text: Legacy Outlook for Mac: check before your mail stops

Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. That date has passed, so check which Outlook you open today. If your mail runs on Exchange On-Premises, legacy Outlook keeps working until October 9, 2029.

blocks.title: Switch to the new Outlook
blocks.text: Open legacy Outlook for Mac and turn off the Legacy Outlook toggle. If the toggle is missing, use Help > Check for Updates, or update the app from the App Store. The new client is called Outlook for Mac (latest version).

Lazur works with the mail app that is open on your Mac. It can explain a message, point at the reply button in a window, or draft text for you. It cannot switch Outlook versions for you. You flip that toggle yourself.
Setting up Lazur before the busy part of the week

Start with the [download page](/download). Open Lazur once, then allow the screen and microphone access that macOS asks for. Lazur needs to see your screen to point and explain. It needs the microphone to hear you while you hold the keys.

items: Open Lazur and allow the screen and microphone access that macOS asks for.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about the sheet in front of you, such as what a column means.
Hold fn in any text box and dictate a short note. Clean text lands at the cursor.
Ask a guide question, such as how to sort a column, and wait for it to pause between steps.
Try one research job on a public page you are allowed to read.

blocks.text: Lazur starts with a trial that needs no credit card. Plans are listed on the [pricing page](/pricing), with monthly and annual options. Check it for the current terms before you decide. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.
Worked example: checking pickup against last year in Excel

Say you open a pickup sheet for next month. Dates run down the left side. Pickup, pace and last year's figures sit in columns across the top. You want to know which dates are behind last year. You do not want to read every row to find out.

Hold ⌥⌘ and ask where the pickup column is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around the header. Then ask what the pace column means. Lazur explains it out loud, in plain words, from what it can read on your screen. You still decide what the change means for your rates.

Lazur reads only what is visible. If a column is cut off or hidden, it cannot see it. Scroll so the header and the first rows show before you ask. Then ask again. This one habit prevents most wrong answers.
Google Sheets for shared pickup and forecast files

Google Sheets runs in Chrome or Safari, so Lazur helps with it the way it helps with any web page. It is common for shared forecasts, because sales and finance open the same file. Ask Lazur to explain a formula, point at the cell you mean, or walk you through a change. The [Google Sheets page](/apps/google-sheets) covers the basics.
Shared files create their own mistakes. These show up in rate and pickup files again and again.

items: Sorting one column and not the others, which pulls dates away from their rates. The [sort guide](/how-to/sort-data-by-column-in-google-sheets) shows the safe way.
Freezing the wrong row, so the headers scroll out of view. The [freeze guide](/how-to/freeze-the-top-row-in-google-sheets) fixes that.
Editing a forecast while someone else edits the same cell.
Pasting a whole export when you only need one column.

blocks.text: For each fix, ask Lazur to guide you. It waits for each click, so you keep control of the file. It will not sort or freeze the sheet for you.
Gmail: drafting sales and group replies without retyping

Sales and marketing send a steady stream of requests. A typical one asks for a rate on a date, a group pickup update, or a view on a promotion. Hold fn in the compose box and dictate your points. Lazur types clean text at your cursor, so you skip the blank page.

Use draft when you want a fuller reply. Tell Lazur the points, the tone and the deadline. It writes the text and types it where your cursor sits. Read every line before you send. Check the dates, the group name and the rate code.

blocks.title: Read before you send
blocks.text: Lazur does not click Send for you. Read the reply, check the rate and dates, then send it yourself. If the reply should go out later, use the [schedule guide](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail).
Research and competitor rates in Chrome

Some questions take longer than a quick answer. Ask Lazur to research a set of public rate pages, and it runs the job in its own Chrome tabs. It returns a summary and a report when it finishes. Those tabs are not the ones you are working in.

Keep research to pages you are allowed to read. Check the site's terms before you point an automated job at it. A rate shown on a public booking page is different from data behind a partner sign-in. Ask your revenue lead before you pull partner data.
Guest and contract data: follow your hotel's rules

Your hotel decides what data can leave its systems. Guest names, payment details, group contracts and negotiated corporate rates often fall under company policy. Lazur sends audio and a screenshot to AI providers to answer you. What is on screen when you ask goes to those providers.

Follow your employer's rules on guest and contract data before you ask about them. If the policy says no, mask names and use totals instead. Lazur's privacy notes say content is never used to train AI models, but that does not replace your hotel's policy. This page does not claim any certification or compliance status for Lazur. Ask your IT or privacy lead what your property allows.
What the numbers do not tell you

One figure travels widely. A Revenue Hub article cites an unnamed survey in which 60% of respondents believed they could save 6 or more hours a week by automating manual tasks. That measures belief about savings, not time spent. Treat it as a hint about where the work sits, not a forecast for your hotel.

Job data is thin too. The BLS does not track revenue managers as a separate job. Its lodging manager figures show about 54,800 jobs in 2025 and a median pay of $69,250 in May 2025. Those numbers are a proxy for the role, not a count of it.
Common mistakes when you first use Lazur on forecast work

items: Asking about a whole workbook at once. Ask about one sheet, one column or one chart, so the answer stays useful.
Forgetting that Lazur sees only what is on screen. Scroll to the part you mean before you hold the keys.
Accepting a formula explanation without a test. Ask for the logic, then check one row you already know.
Dictating rate codes or room type codes and not checking them. Dictation is fast, but codes need a read.
Pasting guest or contract details before you check your hotel's policy.

blocks.text: Next steps for the first week

Pick one recurring task. Most revenue managers start with the pickup check, a formula question or the morning email. Use Lazur for that task all week. Then add the next one. Notice where it saves you a trip to another window, and where it does not help.

For more on the Excel side, read [Excel for hotel revenue managers on Mac](/for/hotel-revenue-managers/excel). When you are ready, the [download page](/download) has the app. The trial starts when you first open it.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin for my property management system?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It works with whatever is open on your Mac, including browser-based systems. It points, explains and guides. It does not log into a system or change its settings for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons in Excel, Sheets or Gmail for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at buttons, explains what they do, and guides you one click at a time while it waits for each click. It can also draft text and type it at your cursor. You do the clicking and the sending.

faq.question: What Mac do I need for Lazur and Office?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned but not available. For Office, Microsoft says macOS Sonoma or later is required starting with the September 2025 update, version 16.101.

faq.question: Can Lazur see guest names in my reservation exports?
faq.answer: It can see what is on your screen while you hold the keys, so yes, if the names are visible. Lazur sends audio and a screenshot to AI providers to answer you. Your hotel's policy decides whether those names may appear at all. Mask them first if the policy says so.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: There is a trial that needs no credit card. Pro and Power are paid plans with monthly and annual options. The pricing page lists current prices and AI action limits, so check it before you decide. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.

faq.question: Can Lazur work out RevPAR for my hotel?
faq.answer: It can explain RevPAR and walk you through the formula. It works from numbers you show it on screen. It does not pull your data from a property system by itself, so check any result against your own report.

faq.question: Which Outlook should I use for hotel sales email?
faq.answer: Use Outlook for Mac (latest version) if you can. Legacy Outlook for Mac stopped working with Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. Turn off the Legacy Outlook toggle in the app, or update it from the App Store.

faq.question: Does research with Lazur touch the tabs I am working in?
faq.answer: No. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report when it finishes. Check each site's terms before you point a job at it, and keep to pages you are allowed to read.

faq.question: Is the BLS count a good measure of revenue manager jobs?
faq.answer: Not really. The BLS does not track revenue managers separately, so its lodging manager figures act as a proxy. Use them for the wider field, not as a headcount of revenue roles.
